title: Ship defensive CSS for dynamic content
principle: Ahmad Shadeed’s Defensive CSS (ishadeed.com → defensivecss.dev): write CSS that survives unexpected content—long titles, odd image ratios, extra flex items—instead of styling only the happy-path mock. For AI UI work, treat every generated layout as hostile until proven robust.
procedure: List failure modes: overflow text, missing images, 1 vs 12 items, RTL, zoom.
For each component, add a defensive rule (wrap, min/max, object-fit, gap, line-clamp with escape).
Prefer flex-wrap / auto-fit patterns over fixed counts assumed by the mock.
Add CSS variable fallbacks where tokens may be missing.
QA with ugly content fixtures, not lorem-perfect strings.
examplePrompts:
Apply Defensive CSS (Shadeed / defensivecss.dev) to this component set:
- Long titles must wrap or truncate without breaking siblings.
- Images: object-fit + fixed aspect so distortion can’t wreck the card.
- Flex/grid: wrap or scroll when item count exceeds the mock.
- Provide CSS variable fallbacks.
Return before/after snippets + the failure mode each fix covers.
Generate three hostile content fixtures (emoji-heavy title, 2KB bio, 0.5× image) and harden the CSS until the layout holds.
promptWhy: Names concrete failure modes so the model doesn’t ‘prettify’ only the screenshot case.
Fixtures force proof—AI often claims robustness without testing.
tips: Built on Shadeed’s earlier ‘just in case’ mindset essays.
Quiet Folio: defense is craft, not chrome.

workedExamples.title: Card title nuke
workedExamples.before: One-line title; AI CSS uses nowrap + fixed height—long titles collide.
workedExamples.after: Wrap with line-clamp(2) + min-height; siblings use gap not absolute offsets.
workedExamples.body: Classic defensive tip: plan for long content.

workedExamples.title: Flex row of ‘exactly 4’
workedExamples.before: Four equal columns; fifth item from CMS overflows off-screen.
workedExamples.after: flex-wrap + min widths; or horizontal scroll with visible cue.

workedExamples.title: Broken hero image
workedExamples.body: Unexpected aspect ratio: lock box with aspect-ratio + object-fit:cover so layout geometry stays.

antiPatterns: Styling only the Figma-perfect string lengths.
Fixed pixel heights that clip real copy.
Assuming image dimensions match the mock forever.
